sources.claim: World Economic Forum, Future of Jobs Report 2025 (January 2025): based on a survey of more than 1,000 employers, it projects 170 million roles created and 92 million displaced worldwide by 2030 (a net 78 million). These are survey-based projections.

BLS Occupational Outlook Handbook, data scientists: employment is projected to grow 34 percent from 2024 to 2034, much faster than the 3 percent average for all occupations. A projection, not a guarantee. The course quotes no pay figures and no credential requirements.

sections.skill: Read an employment forecast as a projection with assumptions

questions.prompt: What is an employment forecast?

choices.text: A guarantee that a certain number of jobs will exist, which employers must legally meet

questions.intro: An employment FORECAST or PROJECTION estimates future jobs based on ASSUMPTIONS: about the economy, technology, population and how employers behave. It is not a promise. Read forecasts by asking: Who made it, and how (a survey of employers, a statistical model)? What period and place does it cover? What does it count? Example: the World Economic Forum's Future of Jobs Report 2025, based on a survey of more than 1,000 employers, projected 170 million roles created and 92 million displaced worldwide by 2030, a net 78 million. Different forecasts often disagree.

sections.skill: Compare a jobs forecast with a weather forecast

questions.prompt: What does "70% chance of rain" mean?

choices.text: Rain is likely but not certain
It will rain for exactly 70% of the day, starting from the early morning hours

questions.correct_answer: Rain is likely but not certain
questions.intro: A WEATHER FORECAST of "70% chance of rain" is useful but not certain. It is based on models and data, it covers a particular place and time, and different services sometimes disagree. A jobs forecast is similar: based on assumptions and methods, for a particular place and period, and not a promise. You bring an umbrella based on a weather forecast; you plan your learning using jobs forecasts, without treating them as certain.

questions.prompt: A global net gain is projected. Could some workers still lose out?

choices.text: Yes; losses can be hidden in a net figure

questions.intro: Large numbers can hide important details. A global "net gain" can include big losses for particular workers, places or roles. Percent growth from a small base can sound huge while adding few jobs. A government projection, such as the US Bureau of Labor Statistics (BLS) estimate that data scientist employment will grow 34 percent from 2024 to 2034, uses its own method and period. Compare like with like, and treat every forecast as one input to your decisions, not a guarantee.
